heard: The upper clouds of Uranus smell like rotten eggs! Astronomers long assumed ammonia gas dominated the giant planet. Even NASA's Voyager 2 flyby couldn't identify what was up there. Then Hawaii's Gemini North telescope analyzed reflected sunlight off the clouds. Instruments detected faint spectral lines of toxic hydrogen sulfide. Unlike Jupiter's ammonia clouds, Uranus formed cold enough to freeze sulfur. In that minus 200-degree atmosphere, nobody could ever smell it. You'd freeze and suffocate long before catching a single whiff.
